passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with respect the sacred offerings that the Israelites have consecrated to Me, so that they do not profane My holy name. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Aaron and his sons.
Aaron and his sons are priests.
The LORD told them to treat the sacred offerings with respect.
The Israelites have consecrated these offerings to the LORD.
Aaron and his sons must not profane the LORD’s holy name.
The Israelites make these offerings holy for the LORD.
The LORD is the one who is holy.
The LORD is the one who makes them holy.
The LORD said, “I am the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְאֶל־ בָּנָ֗יו וְיִנָּֽזְרוּ֙ מִקָּדְשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלֹ֥א יְחַלְּל֖וּ אֶת־ שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵ֧ם מַקְדִּשִׁ֛ים לִ֖י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Tell them that for the generations to come, if any of their descendants in a state of uncleanness approaches the sacred offerings that the Israelites consecrate to the LORD, that person must be cut off from My presence. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave Moses a command for Aaron and his sons.
Aaron and his sons are priests.
God told Moses to speak to them for all generations.
God said: If any descendant of Aaron is unclean, he must not approach the sacred offerings.
The Israelites set apart these offerings for the LORD.
If an unclean priest comes near these offerings, he must be cut off from God's presence.
God said: I am the LORD.
passages.original: אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם לְדֹרֹ֨תֵיכֶ֜ם כָּל־ אִ֣ישׁ׀ אֲשֶׁר־ יִקְרַ֣ב מִכָּל־ זַרְעֲכֶ֗ם אֶל־ הַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְדִּ֤ישׁוּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְטֻמְאָת֖וֹ עָלָ֑יו וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֧פֶשׁ הַהִ֛וא מִלְּפָנַ֖י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: If a descendant of Aaron has a skin disease or a discharge, he may not eat the sacred offerings until he is clean. Whoever touches anything defiled by a corpse or by a man who has an emission of semen, or whoever touches a crawling creature or a person that makes him unclean, whatever the uncleanness may be— the man who touches any of these will remain unclean until evening. He must not eat from the sacred offerings unless he has bathed himself with water.
passages.sermon:
Aaron was the first high priest of Israel.
His descendants are the priests of Israel.
A priest from Aaron’s family may have a skin disease.
A priest from Aaron’s family may have a bodily discharge.
If a priest has a skin disease or a discharge, he must not eat the sacred offerings.
He must wait until he is clean.
A priest may touch something that is defiled by a dead body.
A priest may touch a man who has an emission of semen.
A priest may touch a crawling creature that makes him unclean.
A priest may touch a person who makes him unclean in any way.
If a priest touches any of these things, he becomes unclean until evening.
He must not eat from the sacred offerings while he is unclean.
He may eat from the sacred offerings only after he has washed his body with water.
passages.original: אִ֣ישׁ אִ֞ישׁ מִזֶּ֣רַע אַהֲרֹ֗ן וְה֤וּא צָר֙וּעַ֙ א֣וֹ זָ֔ב בַּקֳּדָשִׁים֙ לֹ֣א יֹאכַ֔ל עַ֖ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְהָ֑ר וְהַנֹּגֵ֙עַ֙ בְּכָל־ טְמֵא־ נֶ֔פֶשׁ א֣וֹ אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ תֵּצֵ֥א מִמֶּ֖נּוּ שִׁכְבַת־ זָֽרַע׃ אוֹ־ אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִגַּ֔ע בְּכָל־ שֶׁ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְמָא־ ל֑וֹ א֤וֹ בְאָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִטְמָא־ ל֔וֹ לְכֹ֖ל טֻמְאָתֽוֹ׃ נֶ֚פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּגַּע־ בּ֔וֹ וְטָמְאָ֖ה עַד־ הָעָ֑רֶב וְלֹ֤א יֹאכַל֙ מִן־ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים כִּ֛י אִם־ רָחַ֥ץ בְּשָׂר֖וֹ בַּמָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: When the sun has set, he will become clean, and then he may eat from the sacred offerings, for they are his food.
passages.sermon:
A priest must be clean to eat the sacred offerings.
He becomes clean after the sun sets.
After sunset, he may eat from the sacred offerings.
The sacred offerings are his food.
passages.original: וּבָ֥א הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וְטָהֵ֑ר וְאַחַר֙ יֹאכַ֣ל מִן־ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים כִּ֥י לַחְמ֖וֹ הֽוּא׃

passages.text: He must not eat anything found dead or torn by wild animals, which would make him unclean. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A priest must not eat any animal that died by itself.
A priest must not eat any animal torn by wild animals.
These things make him unclean.
I am the LORD.
passages.original: נְבֵלָ֧ה וּטְרֵפָ֛ה לֹ֥א יֹאכַ֖ל לְטָמְאָה־ בָ֑הּ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The priests must keep My charge, lest they bear the guilt and die because they profane it. I am the LORD who sanctifies them.
passages.sermon:
The priests must obey My command.
They must not break My law.
If they break it, they will be guilty.
If they are guilty, they may die.
They may die because they treated My law as unholy.
I am the LORD.
I make the priests holy.
passages.original: וְשָׁמְר֣וּ אֶת־ מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֗י וְלֹֽא־ יִשְׂא֤וּ עָלָיו֙ חֵ֔טְא וּמֵ֥תוּ ב֖וֹ כִּ֣י יְחַלְּלֻ֑הוּ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מְקַדְּשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: No one outside a priest’s family may eat the sacred offering, nor may the guest of a priest or his hired hand eat it.
passages.sermon:
A priest is a man chosen by God to serve Him.
A sacred offering is food set apart for God.
No one outside a priest’s family may eat the sacred offering.
A guest living with a priest may not eat the sacred offering.
A hired worker of a priest may not eat the sacred offering.
passages.original: וְכָל־ זָ֖ר לֹא־ יֹ֣אכַל קֹ֑דֶשׁ תּוֹשַׁ֥ב כֹּהֵ֛ן וְשָׂכִ֖יר לֹא־ יֹ֥אכַל קֹֽדֶשׁ׃

passages.text: But if a priest buys a slave with his own money, or if a slave is born in his household, that slave may eat his food.
passages.sermon: A priest may buy a slave with his own money.\r\nThat slave may eat the priest’s food.\r\nA slave born in the priest’s household may also eat the priest’s food.
passages.original: וְכֹהֵ֗ן כִּֽי־ יִקְנֶ֥ה נֶ֙פֶשׁ֙ קִנְיַ֣ן כַּסְפּ֔וֹ ה֖וּא יֹ֣אכַל בּ֑וֹ וִילִ֣יד בֵּית֔וֹ הֵ֖ם יֹאכְל֥וּ בְלַחְמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If the priest’s daughter is married to a man other than a priest, she is not to eat of the sacred contributions.
passages.sermon:
A priest is a man chosen by God to serve Him.
A priest’s daughter is part of his family.
If the priest’s daughter marries a man who is not a priest, she leaves her father’s household.
She is now part of her husband’s family.
She must not eat the sacred offerings.
The sacred offerings are only for the priest’s household.
passages.original: וּבַת־ כֹּהֵ֔ן כִּ֥י תִהְיֶ֖ה לְאִ֣ישׁ זָ֑ר הִ֕וא בִּתְרוּמַ֥ת הַקֳּדָשִׁ֖ים לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽל׃

passages.text: But if a priest’s daughter with no children becomes widowed or divorced and returns to her father’s house, she may share her father’s food as in her youth. But no outsider may share it.
passages.sermon:
A priest is a man who serves God in the sanctuary.
A priest has a daughter.
The daughter was married.
Her husband died or divorced her.
She has no children.
She returns to live in her father’s house.
She may eat her father’s food again.
She may eat the special food given to priests, just as she did when she was young.
No outsider may eat this food.
Only those in the priest’s household may eat it.
passages.original: וּבַת־ כֹּהֵן֩ כִּ֨י תִהְיֶ֜ה אַלְמָנָ֣ה וּגְרוּשָׁ֗ה וְזֶרַע֮ אֵ֣ין לָהּ֒ וְשָׁבָ֞ה אֶל־ בֵּ֤ית אָבִ֙יהָ֙ כִּנְעוּרֶ֔יהָ מִלֶּ֥חֶם אָבִ֖יהָ תֹּאכֵ֑ל וְכָל־ זָ֖ר לֹא־ יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: If anyone eats a sacred offering in error, he must add a fifth to its value and give the sacred offering to the priest.
passages.sermon:
A sacred offering is a special gift set apart for God.
A priest receives the sacred offering.
If any person eats a sacred offering by mistake, he has done wrong.
He must pay back the value of what he ate.
He must add one fifth more to the value.
He must give the total amount to the priest.
passages.original: וְאִ֕ישׁ כִּֽי־ יֹאכַ֥ל קֹ֖דֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָ֑ה וְיָסַ֤ף חֲמִֽשִׁיתוֹ֙ עָלָ֔יו וְנָתַ֥ן לַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת־ הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

passages.text: The priests must not profane the sacred offerings that the Israelites present to the LORD by allowing the people to eat the sacred offerings and thus to bear the punishment for guilt. For I am the LORD who sanctifies them.”
passages.sermon:
The priests serve the LORD.
The priests must not treat the sacred offerings of the Israelites as common.
The Israelites bring these offerings to the LORD.
The priests must not let people eat the sacred offerings in the wrong way.
If people eat the sacred offerings wrongly, they will bear guilt.
I am the LORD.
I make the Israelites holy.
passages.original: וְלֹ֣א יְחַלְּל֔וּ אֶת־ קָדְשֵׁ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ יָרִ֖ימוּ לַיהוָֽה׃ וְהִשִּׂ֤יאוּ אוֹתָם֙ עֲוֺ֣ן אַשְׁמָ֔ה בְּאָכְלָ֖ם אֶת־ קָדְשֵׁיהֶ֑ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מְקַדְּשָֽׁם׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to Aaron and his sons and all the Israelites and tell them, ‘Any man of the house of Israel or any foreign resident who presents a gift for a burnt offering to the LORD, whether to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, must offer an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats in order for it to be accepted on your behalf.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a message.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Aaron.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Aaron’s sons.
The LORD told Moses to speak to all the Israelites.
The LORD told Moses to give them this command.
Any man from the house of Israel may bring an offering to the LORD.
Any foreign resident living among the Israelites may also bring an offering to the LORD.
A man may bring an offering to fulfill a vow.
A man may bring an offering as a freewill gift.
If a man brings a burnt offering to the LORD, he must follow this rule.
He must offer a male animal without blemish.
The animal may be from the cattle.
The animal may be from the sheep.
The animal may be from the goats.
The animal must have no defect.
The LORD will accept the offering only if it is perfect.
The LORD will accept the offering only if it is a male.
The LORD will accept the offering only if it is from cattle, sheep, or goats.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְאֶל־ בָּנָ֗יו וְאֶל֙ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֣ישׁ אִישׁ֩ מִבֵּ֨ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וּמִן־ הַגֵּ֣ר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְרִ֤יב קָרְבָּנוֹ֙ לְכָל־ נִדְרֵיהֶם֙ וּלְכָל־ נִדְבוֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ יַקְרִ֥יבוּ לַיהוָ֖ה לְעֹלָֽה׃ לִֽרְצֹנְכֶ֑ם תָּמִ֣ים זָכָ֔ר בַּבָּקָ֕ר בַּכְּשָׂבִ֖ים וּבָֽעִזִּֽים׃

passages.text: You must not present anything with a defect, because it will not be accepted on your behalf.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions to the Israelites about offerings.
God said, “Do not bring any animal with a defect as an offering.
Do not present anything that is damaged or imperfect.
If you bring a defective offering, I will not accept it for you.
Only perfect offerings are acceptable to Me.”
passages.original: כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ בּ֥וֹ מ֖וּם לֹ֣א תַקְרִ֑יבוּ כִּי־ לֹ֥א לְרָצ֖וֹן יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: When a man presents a peace offering to the LORD from the herd or flock to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, it must be without blemish or defect to be acceptable.
passages.sermon:
A man may bring a peace offering to the LORD.
He may bring it from the herd or from the flock.
He may bring it to fulfill a vow.
He may bring it as a freewill offering.
The animal must be without blemish.
The animal must have no defect.
Only then will the LORD accept the offering.
passages.original: וְאִ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־ יַקְרִ֤יב זֶֽבַח־ שְׁלָמִים֙ לַיהוָ֔ה לְפַלֵּא־ נֶ֙דֶר֙ א֣וֹ לִנְדָבָ֔ה בַּבָּקָ֖ר א֣וֹ בַצֹּ֑אן תָּמִ֤ים יִֽהְיֶה֙ לְרָצ֔וֹן כָּל־ מ֖וּם לֹ֥א יִהְיֶה־ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You are not to present to the LORD any animal that is blind, injured, or maimed, or anything with a running sore, a festering rash, or a scab; you must not put any of these on the altar as an offering made by fire to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for offerings.
God required animals for offerings to be without defects.
You must not bring a blind animal to the LORD.
You must not bring an injured animal to the LORD.
You must not bring a maimed animal to the LORD.
You must not bring an animal with a running sore to the LORD.
You must not bring an animal with a festering rash to the LORD.
You must not bring an animal with a scab to the LORD.
You must not put any of these animals on the altar for the LORD.
You must not offer any of these as a burnt offering to the LORD.
passages.original: עַוֶּרֶת֩ א֨וֹ שָׁב֜וּר אוֹ־ חָר֣וּץ אֽוֹ־ יַבֶּ֗לֶת א֤וֹ גָרָב֙ א֣וֹ יַלֶּ֔פֶת לֹא־ תַקְרִ֥יבוּ אֵ֖לֶּה לַיהוָ֑ה וְאִשֶּׁ֗ה לֹא־ תִתְּנ֥וּ מֵהֶ֛ם עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You may present as a freewill offering an ox or sheep that has a deformed or stunted limb, but it is not acceptable in fulfillment of a vow.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions for offerings.
God said you may bring an ox or a sheep as an offering.
If the ox or sheep has a deformed limb, you may give it as a freewill offering.
If the ox or sheep has a stunted limb, you may give it as a freewill offering.
But you may not use a deformed or stunted animal to fulfill a vow.
God will not accept a deformed or stunted animal for a vow.
passages.original: וְשׁ֥וֹר וָשֶׂ֖ה שָׂר֣וּעַ וְקָל֑וּט נְדָבָה֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ וּלְנֵ֖דֶר לֹ֥א יֵרָצֶֽה׃

passages.text: You are not to present to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut; you are not to sacrifice them in your land.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for offerings.
God required animals for sacrifice to be without defect.
You must not offer any animal to the LORD if its testicles are bruised.
You must not offer any animal to the LORD if its testicles are crushed.
You must not offer any animal to the LORD if its testicles are torn.
You must not offer any animal to the LORD if its testicles are cut.
You must not do this in your land.
You must not sacrifice such animals anywhere in Israel.
passages.original: וּמָע֤וּךְ וְכָתוּת֙ וְנָת֣וּק וְכָר֔וּת לֹ֥א תַקְרִ֖יבוּ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וּֽבְאַרְצְכֶ֖ם לֹ֥א תַעֲשֽׂוּ׃

passages.text: Neither you nor a foreigner shall present food to your God from any such animal. They will not be accepted on your behalf, because they are deformed and flawed.’ ”
passages.sermon:
You must not present food to your God from any of these animals.
A foreigner must not present food to your God from any of these animals.
These animals are deformed.
These animals have flaws.
God will not accept them for you.
passages.original: וּמִיַּ֣ד בֶּן־ נֵכָ֗ר לֹ֥א תַקְרִ֛יבוּ אֶת־ לֶ֥חֶם אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם מִכָּל־ אֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֣י מָשְׁחָתָ֤ם בָּהֶם֙ מ֣וּם בָּ֔ם לֹ֥א יֵרָצ֖וּ לָכֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “When an ox, a sheep, or a goat is born, it must remain with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on, it will be acceptable as an offering made by fire to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
He gave Moses instructions.
When an ox is born, follow these rules.
When a sheep is born, follow these rules.
When a goat is born, follow these rules.
The newborn animal must stay with its mother for seven days.
Do not separate the animal from its mother during these seven days.
From the eighth day onward, you may offer the animal to the LORD.
The animal will be accepted as an offering made by fire to the LORD after the seventh day.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ שׁ֣וֹר אוֹ־ כֶ֤שֶׂב אוֹ־ עֵז֙ כִּ֣י יִוָּלֵ֔ד וְהָיָ֛ה שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים תַּ֣חַת אִמּ֑וֹ וּמִיּ֤וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי֙ וָהָ֔לְאָה יֵרָצֶ֕ה לְקָרְבַּ֥ן אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: But you must not slaughter an ox or a sheep on the same day as its young.
passages.sermon:
God gave a law to the Israelites.
God spoke to Moses.
God said this law about animals for sacrifice.
Do not kill an ox and its young on the same day.
Do not kill a sheep and its young on the same day.
Each animal and its offspring must not be slaughtered together in one day.
passages.original: וְשׁ֖וֹר אוֹ־ שֶׂ֑ה אֹת֣וֹ וְאֶת־ בְּנ֔וֹ לֹ֥א תִשְׁחֲט֖וּ בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: When you sacrifice a thank offering to the LORD, offer it so that it may be acceptable on your behalf.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave instructions to the Israelites.
The LORD is holy.
The LORD brought the Israelites out of Egypt.
The LORD is their God.
When you offer a thank offering to the LORD, do it in the right way.
Offer your sacrifice so the LORD will accept it.
Make sure your offering pleases the LORD.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ תִזְבְּח֥וּ זֶֽבַח־ תּוֹדָ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה לִֽרְצֹנְכֶ֖ם תִּזְבָּֽחוּ׃

passages.text: It must be eaten that same day. Do not leave any of it until morning. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God gave a command about thank offerings.
Eat the thank offering on the same day you sacrifice it.
Do not leave any of the offering until morning.
I am the LORD.
passages.original: בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ יֵאָכֵ֔ל לֹֽא־ תוֹתִ֥ירוּ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד־ בֹּ֑קֶר אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You are to keep My commandments and practice them. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the Israelites.
God gives commandments to the Israelites.
God tells the Israelites to keep His commandments.
God tells the Israelites to do His commandments.
God says, “I am the LORD.”
passages.original: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֙ מִצְוֺתַ֔י וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You must not profane My holy name. I must be acknowledged as holy among the Israelites. I am the LORD who sanctifies you, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD brought you out of the land of Egypt.
The LORD made you His people.
The LORD makes you holy.
Do not profane the holy name of the LORD.
Acknowledge the LORD as holy among the Israelites.
The LORD is the one who sanctifies you.
The LORD is your God.
passages.original: וְלֹ֤א תְחַלְּלוּ֙ אֶת־ שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֔י וְנִ֨קְדַּשְׁתִּ֔י בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מְקַדִּשְׁכֶֽם׃ הַמּוֹצִ֤יא אֶתְכֶם֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לִהְי֥וֹת לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִ֑ים אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃פ
